The story effectively balances the compression and stretching of time to serve its emotional arc. The author compresses larger spans of time—such as the months from February to May when the recurring dreams happen, the intervening week of awkwardness between Daniel and Isabel ("like two people carrying a ladder through a narrow house"), and the week leading up to their river outing—into just a few sentences. This keeps the narrative moving briskly past the routine days. Conversely, time is slowed down and "stretched" during the pivotal emotional beats: the Sunday morning breakfast conversation, the moment on the stairs when Daniel discovers the keys and recalls the memory of the Wye, and the final scene in the canoe. This thoughtful pacing ensures that the reader spends the most time in the moments of highest psychological and relational significance.
